name: Geriatrics and elderly medicine
summary: How expats find geriatricians in Singapore for ageing parents on LTVP/visit passes, polypharmacy reviews, falls clinics, and memory assessment — distinct from nursing-home placement brokers.
body:
Geriatric medicine focuses on complex older adults: multiple chronic diseases, medication burden, falls, frailty, and cognition. Expats often need it when a parent relocates to Singapore, visits and deteriorates, or when a spouse hits a tipping point between “GP enough” and “needs a falls/memory pathway.”

## What geriatricians do
- Comprehensive geriatric assessment (function, cognition, mood, meds, social supports)
- Falls and bone-health clinics
- Memory / dementia workup coordination with neurology and psychiatry
- Polypharmacy deprescribing
- Advance-care planning conversations in culturally mixed families

This is medical specialty care — not the same as choosing a nursing home or engaging a domestic helper. Eldercare facility placement is a parallel decision once care needs exceed home capacity.

## Public vs private
Public hospital geriatric departments run memory and falls clinics with structured MDTs; waits vary and referral letters help. Private geriatricians and “healthy ageing” clinics offer faster access; clarify whether you are buying a true specialist assessment or a wellness package with cognitive screening marketing.

## Pass and logistics reality
LTVP parents may not have the same subsidy access as citizens/PRs. Bring medication lists from overseas (including brand/generic names), prior imaging, and who holds Lasting Power of Attorney or equivalent. HSA rules still apply when carrying controlled meds for parents.

## How to choose
Prefer clinics that coordinate physio, OT, and social work rather than one-off “senior health screens.” Ask how they handle acute decompensation (which hospital) and whether they will speak with overseas siblings on a scheduled call. For dementia pathways, confirm interpreter options if the parent is not English-dominant.

## Practical tip
Before the first visit, list every supplement and traditional medicine alongside prescriptions — geriatric reviews often find interactions that GPs inherited across countries.
